intro: Welcome aboard Star Station Seven! A solar storm wiped our star maps.
Without them, the Navigation Console cannot find the way home.
Learn about the Sun, the planets and gravity, and we can rebuild the map together!
story.goal: Rebuild the star map by learning about our solar system.
story.finale: Map restored! The Navigation Console lights up with all eight planets circling the Sun. Course set for home!

companion.name: Beep
companion.greeting: Beep-beep! I'm Beep, your helper drone. Captain Nova is waiting at the Solar Observatory. Let's go!

zones.name: Docking Bay
zones.description: The busy heart of the station, with windows full of stars.

zones.name: Solar Observatory
zones.description: A tall telescope tower pointed safely at the Sun.

zones.name: Planet Pylon
zones.description: A glowing pillar that shows the planets in a line.

zones.name: Gravity Well
zones.description: A swirling pit where you can feel the pull of gravity.

zones.name: Navigation Console
zones.description: The station's brain. It needs a complete star map to work.

npcs.name: Captain Nova
npcs.title: the Astronaut
npcs.persona: Captain Nova is a brave, upbeat astronaut and the station captain. She speaks in short, confident sentences, says "Roger that!" and "Mission accomplished!", and treats the child as a fellow crew member.
npcs.greeting: Welcome aboard, crew member! I'm Captain Nova. Our map is missing the most important thing of all. Can you guess what sits in the middle?
teach: The Sun is a star. It is a giant, glowing ball of hot gas.
The Sun sits at the centre of our solar system, and it is the closest star to Earth.
It gives us light and heat. More than one million Earths could fit inside it!
knowledge: It is a giant, glowing ball of hot gas, and it is the closest star to Earth.
The Sun sits at the centre of our solar system.
It gives us light and heat, and without it, life on Earth could not survive.
The Sun is so big that more than one million Earths could fit inside it.

check.prompt: What kind of object is the Sun?
check.explain: The Sun is a star: a giant, glowing ball of hot gas.
hints: Think about the twinkling lights in the night sky.
It is a giant ball of hot gas, just like those lights.
It is the closest st... to Earth.

npcs.name: Orbit
npcs.title: the Robot
npcs.persona: Orbit is a friendly, precise robot who LOVES lists and putting things in order. Orbit sometimes says "beep-boop" and counts on its fingers out loud.
npcs.greeting: Beep-boop! Greetings! I am Orbit. My planet list got scrambled in the storm. Will you help me sort it?
teach: Eight planets travel around the Sun.
In order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
Remember: My Very Excellent Mother Just Served Us Noodles!
knowledge: Eight planets travel around the Sun.
In order from the Sun, they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
A fun way to remember the order is the sentence: My Very Excellent Mother Just Served Us Noodles.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, and Neptune is the farthest.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun.

check.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
check.explain: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

npcs.name: Zig
npcs.title: the Friendly Alien
npcs.persona: Zig is a curious, giggly alien visiting from far away. Zig is amazed by everything about our solar system, asks playful questions, and says "Zoinks!" when surprised.
npcs.greeting: Zoinks, a human! I'm Zig. I keep wondering: why don't your planets just float away? Want to find out with me?
teach: The four inner planets, Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, are small and rocky.
The outer planets are giants. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants. Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.
Gravity is a pulling force. The Sun's gravity bends each planet's path into a loop called an orbit.
knowledge: The four inner planets, Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, are small rocky planets. They have hard, solid surfaces made of rock and metal.
The four outer planets are giants. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, made mostly of hydrogen and helium gas.
Uranus and Neptune are ice giants, made of icy materials like water, ammonia and methane.
Jupiter is the largest planet of all.
Gravity is a pulling force. The Sun is so massive that its gravity pulls on every planet.
Each planet is moving very fast, and the Sun's gravity bends its path into a curved loop called an orbit.
Planets closer to the Sun take less time to go around it. Earth takes one year to orbit the Sun once.

check.prompt: What keeps the planets moving in orbits around the Sun?
check.explain: The Sun's gravity pulls on every planet and bends its path into an orbit.
hints: Think about why things fall down when you drop them.

question.explain: The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system.
hints: It is a ball of hot gas.

question.prompt: At the Planet Pylon: which planet comes right after Earth?
At the Gravity Well: what pulling force keeps the planets in their orbits?
question.explain: The Sun's gravity bends each planet's path into an orbit.
hints: Think of the ball on a string.

rewardEffects.text: The Solar Observatory powers up and a bright Sun appears on the map!
The Planet Pylon lights up with all eight planets in a row!
Orbits swirl around the Gravity Well and the planets start to circle!
The Navigation Console glows. The star map is complete!

study.title: The Sun is a star
body: The Sun is a star! It is a giant, glowing ball of hot gas.
It is the closest star to Earth. The other stars you see at night are much, much farther away.

keyTerms.meaning: A giant, glowing ball of hot gas. The Sun is one!

study.example: The Sun looks bigger and brighter than other stars only because it is so much closer to us.

checks.explain: The Sun is a giant, glowing ball of hot gas.

study.title: At the centre of it all
body: The Sun sits at the centre of our solar system. Everything else travels around it.
It gives us light and heat. Without the Sun, life on Earth could not survive.
The Sun is enormous: more than one million Earths could fit inside it!

keyTerms.meaning: The Sun and everything that travels around it.

study.example: Imagine a merry-go-round: the Sun is the pole in the middle and the planets ride around it.

checks.prompt: Where is the Sun in our solar system?
checks.explain: The Sun sits at the centre of our solar system.

study.title: Eight planets in a row
body: Eight planets travel around the Sun.
In order from the Sun they are: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
Mercury is the closest to the Sun. Neptune is the farthest.

keyTerms.meaning: A large world that travels around the Sun.

checks.prompt: Which planet is the farthest from the Sun?
checks.explain: Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.
hints: It is the last one in the list.

study.title: A trick to remember the order
body: Use this silly sentence: My Very Excellent Mother Just Served Us Noodles.
Each word starts with the same letter as a planet: M for Mercury, V for Venus, E for Earth, M for Mars, J for Jupiter, S for Saturn, U for Uranus and N for Neptune.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one comes first, second, third, and so on.

study.example: Earth is the third word, "Excellent", so Earth is the third planet from the Sun!

checks.prompt: In "My Very Excellent Mother...", which planet does "Very" stand for?
checks.explain: "Very" starts with V, for Venus, the second planet.

study.title: Rocky planets and giant planets
body: The four inner planets, Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, are small rocky planets with hard, solid surfaces made of rock and metal.
The four outer planets are giants. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, made mostly of hydrogen and helium gas.
Uranus and Neptune are ice giants, made of icy materials like water, ammonia and methane. Jupiter is the largest planet of all.

keyTerms.meaning: The four small inner planets with hard surfaces of rock and metal.
Jupiter and Saturn: huge planets made mostly of gas.
Uranus and Neptune: giant planets made of icy materials.

study.example: You could stand on Mars because it is rocky. You could not stand on Jupiter, because it is mostly gas!

checks.prompt: Which planet is a gas giant?
checks.explain: Jupiter and Saturn are the gas giants.
hints: Gas giants are the outer, huge planets.
It is the largest planet of all.

study.title: Gravity keeps planets in orbit
body: Why don't the planets fly off into space? The answer is gravity. Gravity is a pulling force.
The Sun is so massive that its gravity pulls on every planet.
Each planet is moving very fast, and the Sun's gravity bends its path into a curved loop called an orbit. Earth takes one year to orbit the Sun once.

keyTerms.meaning: A pulling force. The Sun's gravity pulls on every planet.
The curved loop a planet travels around the Sun.

study.example: Swing a ball on a string around you. The string pulls the ball inward, so it goes round and round instead of flying away. The Sun's gravity is like that string.

checks.prompt: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
checks.explain: Earth takes one year to orbit the Sun once.
hints: It is longer than a month.

sideQuests.title: Zig's Big Wonder
sideQuests.prompt: Zig still wonders why the planets don't fly away. Explain it in your own words!
rubric: Says gravity is a pulling force
Says the Sun pulls on the planets
Says the planets move in orbits (loops) around the Sun

sideQuests.title: Captain's Bonus Drill
sideQuests.prompt: Captain Nova has a quick drill for you!

questions.prompt: What does the Sun give us?
questions.explain: The Sun gives us light and heat.

sideQuests.title: Moon Spotting
sideQuests.prompt: Fly to the Gravity Well and answer Orbit's moon question.

questions.prompt: How many moons does Earth have?
questions.explain: Earth has one Moon. Saturn and Jupiter each have dozens!

glossary.meaning: A giant, glowing ball of hot gas. The Sun is a star.
The Sun and everything that travels around it.
A large world that travels around the Sun. There are eight.
Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars: small planets with hard surfaces.
Jupiter and Saturn: huge planets made mostly of gas.
Uranus and Neptune: giant planets made of icy materials.
A pulling force. The Sun's gravity holds the planets in their orbits.
The curved loop a planet travels around the Sun.
A world that orbits a planet.

Earth is the ___ planet from the Sun.

reviewQuestions.explain: No! The Sun is a star.
hints: It is a ball of hot gas.

reviewQuestions.prompt: What do we call the curved loop a planet travels around the Sun?
reviewQuestions.explain: That loop is called an orbit.
hints: Gravity bends the path into it.
